coverage_credit.reason: Validation shard only; Project-Frankenstein exhaustive denominator remains unfrozen.

observations.claim: gateway/app.py /chat/vision directly imports tools.native_vision.get_vision and calls get_vision().analyze() for uploaded-image analysis.
The same /chat/vision endpoint returns metadata model='frankeye' even though the implementation path immediately above used NativeVision. This is a concrete naming/telemetry drift at the API surface.

agentic/loop.py _capture_visual_context directly imports tools.native_vision.get_vision and uses NativeVision for error-screenshot analysis, confirming NativeVision is wired into agentic error-observation behavior at frozen HEAD.

Repository search for frank-feature-training and feature_trainer.py returned only ext/feature_trainer.py; search for feature-training.service returned no result. The repository therefore does not provide evidence in this shard that the feature trainer service is installed/enabled from tracked code.

synthesis.backend_selection: NativeVision is demonstrably wired into at least the remote vision API and agentic visual error-context path. The earlier counterhypothesis that NativeVision might be an isolated unused file is materially weakened.
synthesis.trainer_activity: The stale FrankEye training ground truth remains a real repository artifact, but active corruption risk is not established because no tracked service enablement/invocation was found. Treat active execution as OPEN, not CURRENT.
synthesis.telemetry_bug: API metadata reports model='frankeye' for a NativeVision-backed request. Any Harness/observability layer that trusts this label can misclassify backend provenance even when execution is correct.
synthesis.level0_lineage: Project-Frankenstein carries at least three distinct states that must not be collapsed: legacy FrankEye implementation, newer NativeVision execution wiring, and stale/legacy naming/self-knowledge artifacts that still say FrankEye.

branch_feedback.harness: Record backend provenance from actual execution identity/version rather than the legacy API label 'frankeye'; add a test that endpoint metadata matches executed backend.
branch_feedback.frank: Separate capability name ('vision') from backend implementation identity and historical aliases.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Encode alias versus supersession explicitly: FrankEye can remain a historical/capability alias while NativeVision is current backend for confirmed call paths.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: Persist execution receipts with backend module/version, not only user-facing model labels.
branch_feedback.claycode: Make perception effect receipts carry semantic backend identity distinct from compatibility/display aliases.

counterhypotheses.claim: Some other visual call paths may still use FrankEye.
counterhypotheses.reason: This shard validates two NativeVision paths, not all vision paths.

counterhypotheses.claim: feature_trainer may be installed/enabled outside tracked repository state.
counterhypotheses.next_test: Requires actual target-machine/systemd/runtime receipt; repository search cannot establish external service state.

negative_results: No tracked feature-training service unit or repository-side invocation was found by the available code-search surface.
No exact Level-0 coverage credit is justified.
No claim is made about target-machine service enablement without runtime evidence.
